2018

 S.D.
 W.P. 2660 (W) of 2018
 (Unlisted)
 Kailindar Ram & Ors.
 Vs.
 The Union of India & Ors.

Mr. Ashoke Banerjee, Sr. Adv.,
 Mr. Rahul Karmakar
 Ms. Gargi Goswami
 ....For the Petitioner.
Mr. Sanajit Kumar Ghosh
....For the Respondent Nos. 1, 2, 3 & 5.
I n v i e w o f t h e u r g e n c y p l e a d e d , l e a v e w a s g r a n t e d t o m o v e
the writ petition as an unlisted motion in the morning.
Pursuant to such leave, the writ petition is taken up for consideration.
The Railway Authorities are represented.

L e a r n e d S e n i o r A d v o c a t e f o r t h e p e t i t i o n e r s s u b m i t s t h a t ,
the petitioners are similarly situated and circumstanced as that of the petitioners of an earlier  writ petition in which the Court had passed an interim order on February 2, 2018.
He  submits that, similar interim order should be passed.
He draws the attention of the Court to the  fact that, the petitioners hold licences issued by officers of the Railways.
Such licences are  still valid.
During the subsistence of such licences, the Railway Authorities ought not to take
any  m e a s u r e t o e v i c t t h e p e t i t i o n e r s .
M o r e o v e r , t h e petitioners are sought to be evicted without the due process of law.
No notice of eviction has been  s e r v e d u p o n t h e p e t i t i o n e r s .
T h e livelihood of the petitioners is at stake.
Consequently, an interim protection is called for.

L e a r n e d A d v o c a t e f o r t h e R a i l w a y A u t h o r i t i e s s u b m i t s t h a t ,
t h e l i c e n c e s t h a t t h e p e t i t i o n e r s s p e a k o f , a r e n o t l i c e n c e s t o o c c u p y a railway property
. The licences are under the Food Standards and Safety Act, which has a  different zone for its operation.

Such licences cannot be pressed into service for the purpose  o f c o n t e n d i n g t h a t , t h e p e t i t i o n e r s a r e e n t i t l e d t o o c c u p y a n y p a r t o r Kailindar Ram & Ors vs The Union Of India & Ors on 5 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37129771/
1 p o r t i o n o f p r o p e r t y b e l o n g i n g t o t h e r a i l w a y s . H e s u b m i t s t h a t , t h e r a i l w a y s h a v e t a k e n a p o l i c y d e c i s i o n t o d o a w a y w i t h c o m m i s s i o n vendors.

In terms of such policy, commission vendors were given the option of absorption, 
s u b j e c t t o s u c h c o m m i s s i o n v e n d o r s f u l f i l l i n g t h e c r i t e r i a l a i d d o w n f o r a b s o r p t i o n i n s u c h p o l i c y .
T h e p e t i t i o n e r s h e r e i n h a v e e i t h e r o p t e d n o t t o b e a b s o r b e d o r d i d n o t satisfy the criteria for the purpose of absorption.

Any interference by the Writ Court at this stage  will prejudice the railway authorities in obtaining possession of the railway property in order t o i m p l e m e n t i t s c a t e r i n g p o l i c y .
H e r e l i e s u p o n t w o d e c i s i o n s o f the Division Bench and submits that, in similar circumstances, the Division Bench had refused to  intervene in favour of the writ petitioners.
The decisions of the Division Bench relied upon by the railway authorities are dated May 3, 2017 passed in M.A.T. 603 of 2017 with CAN 4058 of 2017

sentences.text: Learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners in reply submits that, the  factual scenario obtaining in the two decisions of the Division Bench are different to that of the present facts.
I have considered the rival contentions of the parties and the materials made available on record.

A w r i t i n g d a t e d J a n u a r y 2 5 , 2 0 1 8 i s s u e d b y t h e S e n i o r D i v i s i o n a l C o m m i s s i o n e r M a n a g e r , E a s t e r n R a i l w a y t o t h e G r o u p G e n e r a l M a n a g e r , I R C T C , E a s t e r n Z o n e i s i m p u g n e d i n t h e p r e s e n t w r i t p e t i t i o n . B y s u c h w r i t i n g , r a i l w a y a u t h o r i t i e s a r e o f t h e v i e w that, the stalls/trolleys operated by commission vendors should be taken possession of

so that  the extant catering policy may be implemented.
R e l i a n c e i s p l a c e d o n b e h a l f o f t h e p e t i t i o n e r s t o a b u n c h o f d o c u m e n t s c l a i m i n g t h a t , t h e p e t i t i o n e r s h a v e a l i c e n c e g r a n t e d b y t h e r a i l w a y a u t h o r i t i e s t o o c c u p y a p o r t i o n o f t h e r a i l w a y p r o p e r t y .

T h e s o  c a l l e d l i c n e c e s a r e u n d e r t h e F o o d S t a n d a r d a n d S a f e t y A c t ,
2006.

Such documents although issued by the railway authorities cannot be construed to mean  that, the same grants permission to the awardee of such licences to occupy a part or portion  of the railway property.
Moreover, the petitioners were allowed sufficient opportunity of  a b s o r p t i o n b y t h e r a i l w a y a u t h o r i t i e s i n t e r m s o f t h e i r e x i s t i n g p o l i c y .
E i t h e r t h e p e t i t i o n e r s d i d n o t o p t f o r t h e s a m e o r d i d n o t q u a l i f y f o r a b s o r p t i o n .
T h e p e t i t i o n e r s c a n n o t claim that, they should be allowed to occupy the railway property for eternity.
In such circumstances, prima facie case not being made out and the balance of convenience  and/or inconvenience also not being in favour of the petitioners no interim relief can be granted.
